reason: E2 supports the formation of a nanocrystalline layer and its link to low friction/wear in inert conditions, but E1 only shows that fine grains and residual stress weaken the passive layer in a general processing context, not under sliding tribo-corrosion. The critical premise that the sliding-induced nanocrystalline layer disrupts the passive film and causes accelerated localized corrosion is not directly evidenced by the cited passages.
premises: Sliding contact induces a dynamic nanocrystalline/amorphized surface layer in CoCrFeMnNi
This nanocrystalline layer lowers friction and wear in inert conditions
Residual stress and fine grains weaken the passive layer and reduce corrosion resistance in HEAs
The nanocrystalline layer disrupts passive film integrity, exposing active sites to electrolyte
Accelerated localized corrosion couples with wear to dominate overall degradation
